elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall ...", so all three limbs attach to every expiry and every termination, not only Client-elected termination under Section 14.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months". The request condition is not tied to anticipated expiry only; it is exercisable after any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to Client all data of Client and its customers in TrueLink's possession" — the deadline runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) ends "in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to Client" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening trigger "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) makes assistance available for up to six (6) months, which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Client data in machine-readable form within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination.

reasons: Finding status "missing" is correct: Section 13 only imposes on Client the burden of arranging a new name server (30 days) and hosting environment (60 days) and confirms domain/Client Content ownership; Section 14 merely continues services to month-end. Neither obliges TrueLink to assist, return data, or certify deletion, so the document sat in walk-away territory (no data return).
All six preferred elements are met by the single inserted paragraph, so the redline is position-complete at the preferred level (and, a fortiori, at the fallback level).

Minimality holds: one concise insertion after Section 14, no deletion or paraphrase of existing language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no added remedies or procedures, and no duplication of any existing exit mechanic (there was none).

Because the Agreement has no defined term "Customer Data", specifying "all data of Client and its customers in TrueLink's possession" is necessary scope-setting rather than an extra requirement, and it covers every category of Client data rather than selected named types.
Intent is preserved: the Section 13 Client-side migration deadlines and the Section 14 continuation-of-services mechanic survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference is disturbed.

Drafting caution (not a defect in the checklist): confirm "Credit Data" is a defined term elsewhere in the Agreement; if it is not, lowercase it or delete the illustrative "including Client Content and Credit Data" so the insertion leaves no undefined capitalised term.
